articles.title: ‘Maybe I’m just getting older’: Naomi Osaka’s surprising reaction after US Open exit
articles.summary: Tennis News: Naomi Osaka's US Open campaign came to an end in the fourth round, but the former world No. 1 walked away from Flushing Meadows with a sense of perspe.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka's US Open campaign came to an end in the fourth round, but the former world No. 1 walked away from Flushing Meadows with a sense of perspective rather than disappointment.The two-time US Open champion was beaten by Elena Rybakina in a one-sided contest on Monday, ending a run that had also seen Osaka once again capture attention away from the court with a series of eye-catching fashion statements.Yet when she addressed the media after the defeat, Osaka's focus was less on the loss and more on the bigger picture.Asked whether she was disappointed that her exit meant fans would not get to see some of the other fashion looks she may have planned for later rounds, Osaka admitted there was always something in the works."I think there's always something [laughs]. That's a way that I can have fun and sort of just excite myself also. But I'm honestly not disappointed now. It's a very strange feeling. And last year I wasn't that disappointed either. Amanda just played really insane. Maybe I'm just getting older, but I don't feel sad."‘I'm happy I'm taking losses differently’The four-time Grand Slam champion was then asked whether she was surprised by her reaction to the defeat, given that losses had often affected her more deeply earlier in her career.Osaka said she has learned to process setbacks differently and now looks for lessons rather than dwelling on disappointment."I think I'm happy I'm taking losses differently. I'm trying to learn from them a lot more. Today if I was to say I'm sad, I was sad that I couldn't push off on my foot. I'm sad I couldn't do what I set out to do."The 28-year-old revealed she had been troubled by pain in her leg during the match against Rybakina, which affected her movement on court.Still, she stressed that tennis results no longer define her outlook on life."But for me if I think about my life, my daughter is healthy. Everyone in my family is great. I had an opportunity to play this Slam. I got as far as I could. It's only up from here I guess."Osaka's fashion showcase lights up New YorkAlthough her tournament ended in the fourth round, Osaka remained one of the standout personalities of the event thanks to a string of fashion-forward appearances inspired by basketball culture.With sponsor Nike celebrating the New York Knicks' championship triumph, Osaka unveiled a different look throughout the tournament, working alongside celebrity stylist Law Roach.For her final appearance, she arrived on court wearing a fur-trimmed multicoloured cloak designed by Brooklyn-based label KidSuper."I felt really swaggy when I put it on," Osaka said after the match. "I feel feel like it embodied New York a lot."The outfit also featured a headband inspired by the NBA logo, replacing the traditional basketball player silhouette with a tennis player holding a racket.Earlier in the tournament, Osaka paid tribute to NBA legend Allen Iverson with a dramatic first-round ensemble designed by Who Decides War, featuring a long white tulle skirt, a hooded robe and cornrows beneath a headband reminiscent of Iverson's iconic style.Her second-round look came from Thom Browne and included a flowing white jacket embroidered with crossed tennis rackets, while the mesh fabric of her skirt was designed to resemble a basketball net.For the third round, she wore an oversized Monse outfit that blended a suit jacket and hoodie with flowing fleece trousers, combining businesswear and sportswear aesthetics.‘If I win another Grand Slam, it's not going to change my life’Osaka's comments after the loss reflected a broader shift in how she now views her career and achievements.While still motivated to compete at the highest level, the former world No. 1 suggested that winning another major title would not fundamentally alter her life or sense of fulfilment.Reflecting on everything she has already achieved in the sport, Osaka indicated she no longer measures happiness solely through victories and trophies."Maybe I'm just getting older, but I don't feel sad," Osaka said. "I think, also, if I reflect on my career and the things that I've been able to do, there's nothing that I regret or there's nothing that I'm sad about ... If I win another Grand Slam, it's not going to change my life."For Osaka, the US Open may have ended earlier than she hoped, but her reaction to defeat suggested a player increasingly at peace with both her career and her life beyond tennis.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Zverev de siempre ya está en cuartos de final
articles.standfirst: El alemán vuelve a convencer ante Darderi y es el primero en llegar a las 50 victorias esta temporada
articles.summary: El alemán vuelve a convencer ante Darderi y es el primero en llegar a las 50 victorias esta temporada
articles.body: Alexander Zverev continúa con su temporada estelar en los Grand Slam. Por cuarta vez este año, ha certificado su pase a los cuartos de final de un grande, el único jugador en hacerlo. En esta ocasión, ha derrotado al italiano Luciano Darderi por 6-2, 6-2 y 7-6 (3) en otro gran desempeño. Sascha, que en sus dos primeros partidos en Flushing Meadows llegó a sumar 10 horas en pista, ha cambiado el guion de su torneo. En el duelo de tercera ronda con Tabilo, y hoy ante Darderi, ha conseguido dos valiosas victorias en tres mangas. Cabe recordar que los cuatro partidos diputados hasta el momento del alemán, han sido en el segundo turno nocturno de la Arthur Ashe. Condiciones que parecen sentarle bien al tenista de Hamburgo. Zverev tenía muy claro como salir hoy. Agresivo y enchufado desde el primer punto, más si cabe sabiendo de la pegada que tiene el italiano. Todo estuvo marcado por el servicio del alemán, que elevó su porcentaje de primeros hasta un 72%, adjudicándose 51 de 59 (86%) puntos con una de sus mayores armas. Sascha empezó marcando su terreno rompiendo el saque de su rival en el juego inicial del partido. Las dos primeras mangas siguieron la misma tónica, el alemán, incontestable tanto al servicio como al resto, y Darderi sin saber por donde tirar. Hasta 17 bolas de 'break' llegó a fabricarse el primer cabeza de serie del torneo. El tercer set necesitó del tie-break para decidir el último cuartofinalista del cuadro masculino. El italiano había subido de gran manera en el encuentro de la mano de su mejora al primer servicio. Pero la regularidad del alemán tuvo premio (su récord en tie-breaks en 2026 es de 28-13) y lo cerró por 7-3. Zverev, ya con un nivel más parecido al que le hizo campeón en la tierra de París y finalista en Wimbledon, está entre los ocho mejores del US Open. Con sus 19 cuartos de final, Sascha es el segundo tenista en activo que más veces ha pisado esta ronda. Ya ha superado a Stan Wawrinka (18), y solo tiene por encima a Novak Djokovic (66). Su próximo objetivo será el holandés Botic Van de Zandschulp, que viene de derrotar al lucky-loser Arthur Gea en 5:13 h de partido, el cuarto más largo en la historia del torneo.

articles.title: US Open 2026: Home favourite Coco Gauff wins all-American showdown with Iva Jovic to reach quarter-finals
articles.summary: An impressive victory for Coco Gauff sets up a last-eight meeting with French Open champion Mirra Andreeva; Gauff is aiming to win the US Open for a second time in her career; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
The 22-year-old, who is bidding for a second Flushing Meadows title, overpowered Jovic 6-1, 6-4 on a balmy Labour Day bank holiday night in New York.

A jittery start from the 2023 winner gifted 18-year-old Jovic a break in the first game with a double fault.

But Jovic's nerves were also on show as Gauff raced away with the next six games to take the first set.

Jovic finally held serve at the start of the second but three spectacular Gauff hustles, turning desperate defence into all-out attack, secured a break for 3-2.

The youngster managed to hit straight back, but was then broken to love as Gauff took control before serving out to win in an hour and 33 minutes.

Gauff, who is yet to drop a set so far, made sure to reassure Jovic that her time will come: "Iva's an incredible player, an incredible talent, she plays beyond her years. I'm used to being the younger American!

"I thought today was a good match for me. The first set was really high-level and she raised her level in the second.

"I had some opportunities to maybe get up some early breaks. We're all just happy with how I was able to close the last game out.

"I think I just remember when I was that age, every loss was so low, and every win was so high. I think there's lessons to be learned in the losses.

"She seems a little bit more mature than maybe I was at 18, but I feel like sometimes the losses for me felt so low.

"So I think it's just important getting her to know that she's playing good-level tennis, and I think today it just went my way.

"I am someone who played well young too, so it doesn't always matter. Sometimes it does matter, and you just learn those lessons and I know that she will be in many more fourth rounds and quarters, and she'll capitalise on those moments the next time."

Andreeva up next as quarter-final line-up complete

The impressive victory set up a last-eight meeting with French Open champion Mirra Andreeva, whom Gauff has beaten in all five of their career meetings.

With Gauff's win, the woman's quarter final line-up is set as Aryna Sabalenka plays Linda Noskova and Jessica Pegula takes on Emma Navarro.

Gauff then faces Andreeva, with Qinwen Zheng against Elena Rybakina for a place in the final four at Flushing Meadows.

"It is another tough match," Gauff added. "Mirra is someone that I always have tough matches with and they have leaned my way but every match could have almost gone either way.

"She is obviously in a different mindset now at the top of the game coming off of a Grand Slam win. I expect her to approach the match completely differently than she did in the past."

articles.title: US Open 2026: Alexander Zverev reaches quarter-finals in rare pre-midnight finish in New York
articles.summary: World No 87 Arthur Gea missed out on becoming the first lucky loser to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final as he lost to Botic van de Zandschulp, who awaits as Alexander Zverev's last eight opponent; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
The top-seeded German cruised through the opening two sets before fending off a Darderi fightback in the third to win 6-2 6-2 7-6(3).

It would mark the first time Zverev has finished a match before midnight in New York this tournament having played four successive night-session matches, including two five-setters.

The 2020 finalist, who has previously finished games at times of 1:55am, 2:15am and 1:09am, was able to see the funny side of a rare early night at 11.48pm.

"I don't know what to do with ​myself, because it's before midnight," said Zverev. "I might go to a practice court, or a bar... that was a joke, so ‌relax. I'm feeling happy, compared to the first two matches the level has been going up."

Zverev is the only man to reach the quarter-finals of all four Grand Slams this year and will now face Botic van de Zandschulp in the final four following the Dutchman's win over lucky loser Arthur Gea.

"I ⁠thought that my level was consistent, but he started incredibly well in third set," Zverev added of his performance.

"I barely saw anyone hit so hard so consistently. He ⁠made it very difficult for me. I'm ​happy to be in the quarter-finals and playing this way."

Next opponent Van de Zandschulp had denied France's world No 87 Gea the chance to become the first lucky loser to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final in a 3-6 6-7 (0-7) 7-6 (9-7) 7-6 (7-3) 6-4 win lasting five hours and 13 minutes.

"I think he's an impressive player," said Zverev of Van de Zandschulp. "I think this might be his favourite tournament in the world, because I think he made a few quarter-finals here before. Obviously he knows how to play well on these courts, and I look forward to having a tough battle."

Belgium's Alexander Blockx meanwhile fought through injury to beat Argentina's Francisco Cerundolo and reach his first Grand Slam quarter-final.

The 28th seed clinched a 6-3 4-6 7-5 7-5 victory before admitting he considered retiring hurt due to a rib issue.

"It was really tough from the beginning of the match. I was struggling a lot, especially while serving. It kept getting worse throughout the match," said the 21-year-old.

"I was really close to retiring, to be honest. I was just hanging in there, but if I would have lost the third set, I think the chances were really high of me retiring.

He will now play Karen Khachanov after the Russian's 7-5, 4-6, 6-7 (6), 6-1, 6-4 win over the USA's Learner Tien.

articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz se enteró a última hora de la noche del domingo que su rival en los cuartos del US Open será el local Ben Shelton. El número nueve mundial y octavo cabeza de serie del cuadro se deshizo de Stefanos Tsitsipas en la ronda de octavos. Shelton ha cedido los tres precedentes con el murciano, el último de ellos en los octavos de Roland Garros 2025. El estadounidense viene en forma como lo demuestra su título en el Masters 1000 de Montreal en el inicio de la gira americana de pista dura. Su mejor resultado en el cuarto grande del calendario fueron las semifinales de 2023. El partido de cuartos del US Open entre Carlos Alcaraz y Ben Shelton se disputará este martes 8 de septiembre en la central Arthur Ashe, del Billie Jean King Tennis Center, en el último turno de la sesión nocturna. El partido empezará sobre las 2:30 horas de la madrugada del martes al miércoles en horario peninsular. Tras superar las rondas previas con solvencia, Carlos Alcaraz afronta un duro examen ante el potente servicio de Ben Shelton en el Arthur Ashe, con la mirada puesta en unas semifinales donde se cruzaría con el vencedor del duelo estadounidense entre Frances Tiafoe y Alex Michelsen. Tras superar con solvencia a Tommy Paul en octavos, Carlos Alcaraz (2.º cabeza de serie) afronta este martes los cuartos de final ante el estadounidense Ben Shelton (8). articles.title: US Open 2026: Carlos Alcaraz can end American dreams by beating Ben Shelton, plus Frances Tiafoe or Alex Michelsen, in New York
articles.summary: Three Americans have the chance to become the first home US Open men's champion since 2003. But Carlos Alcaraz stands in the way.
articles.body:
It could be Carlos Alcaraz versus the United States over the next few days.

The Spanish superstar's popularity at the US Open might be severely tested if he single-handedly prevents an American having the chance to become the first home men's singles champion in 23 years.

Three American players - Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen - remain in the draw. All three are in the same half as Alcaraz.

On Tuesday, the defending champion takes on eighth seed Shelton in the quarter-finals.

If the seven-time major winner comes through that blockbuster clash, he will face either Tiafoe or Michelsen in the semi-finals.

And if Alcaraz wins again to reach the Flushing Meadows final, the host nation's long wait for somebody to finally follow in Andy Roddick's 2003 footsteps continues.

Alcaraz says he expects to be facing 24,000 New Yorkers on Arthur Ashe Stadium as well as Shelton, who is looking to reach his second US Open semi-final.

"I think he [will] use the crowd, the people behind him, especially when he's playing here at home," said Alcaraz.

If Ashe can help 23-year-old Shelton earn his first career win over Alcaraz, there is guaranteed to be an American player in the final.

Home stars reaching the men's semi-finals has not been uncommon this century, but only Taylor Fritz has reached the final - two years ago when he lost to Jannik Sinner - since Roddick was beaten by Roger Federer in the 2006 final.

Tiafoe, who is seeded 11th, lost to Fritz in another all-American semi-final and was also eliminated by Alcaraz at the same stage in 2022.

Now the 28-year-old is aiming for a third opportunity to reach his first Grand Slam final.

Tiafoe reached the Cincinnati final last month and, thriving off the energy of the New York crowd, has maintained his momentum.

On what it is like to receive such support, he said: "It's an out-of-body experience, no question. No real explaining that type of feeling.

"It's like you're not even touching the ground at one point. Energy is so high, and it seems like the level of play matches that."

While Tiafoe is one of the sport's great entertainers, 22-year-old Michelsen is more understated.

The world number 46 admits he has been happy to fly "under the radar" at Flushing Meadows while the likes of Tiafoe, Shelton, Fritz and Tommy Paul soak up the attention.

But earning a place in a Grand Slam quarter-final for the first time, and not dropping a set on his way, means Michelsen will find himself under the spotlight on Ashe.

"First, second, third rounds, all matches I'm feeling nerves. It's a human experience," he said.

"But it's just about going out there and managing them to the best of my ability. I feel like I've done that very well."

Six men and women from the United States have reached the last eight at Flushing Meadows this year - the highest tally since 2002 - with three players in each draw.

Along with Tiafoe or Michelsen in the men's, the home fans know they are guaranteed to see at least one American reach the women's semi-finals.

Third seed Jessica Pegula, who is yet to land a major title despite her consistency on the WTA Tour, meets Emma Navarro in another all-American clash on Tuesday.

Coco Gauff - who sits on the other side of the draw - can join Pegula or Navarro by beating Russian fifth seed Mirra Andreeva on Wednesday.

But, unlike the men, there is not a long American drought on the women's side.

Gauff, 22, is looking to win the women's title for the second time, having lifted the trophy in 2023 as a teenager to fulfil the promise she had already long shown.

Pegula, 31, was a beaten finalist in 2024 when she lost to Aryna Sabalenka, who also beat Navarro in the semi-finals that year.

Navarro, 25, has not reached the same stage of a major since, but is rediscovering her best form after stepping back from the tour earlier this season because of health issues.

After beating Russian 21st seed Anna Kalinskaya on Ashe in the last 16, Navarro joked she should have tried getting the home fans on her side before facing Pegula.

"I should have talked to the crowd a little, asking them to come back and cheer me on for that match. I'm definitely going to need them," she said.

articles.title: Wimbledon no acreditará a 'influencers' tras los incidentes en el US Open
articles.standfirst: La 'mala praxis' de los creadores de contenido ha provocado críticas por parte de los tenistas y problemas durante algunos partidos
articles.summary: La 'mala praxis' de los creadores de contenido ha provocado críticas por parte de los tenistas y problemas durante algunos partidos
articles.body: El torneo de Wimbledon no acreditará a 'influencers' y se desmarcará de esta manera de las polémicas surgidas en el actual Abierto de Estados Unidos, donde cerca de un centenar de 'creadores de contenido' fueron acreditados por la organización y provocaron problemas durante la disputa de los partidos. El torneo neoyorquino dio el doble de acreditaciones a 'influencers' de cara a esta edición con el objetivo de atraer a una audiencia mayor, pero las prácticas de los mismos han provocado críticas por parte de los tenistas y problemas durante los partidos. Según medios británicos, la organización de Wimbledon no tiene entre sus planes acreditar a 'influencers' o creadores de contenido, como ha sido la norma habitual hasta ahora. Además, las normas del propio All England Club, el recinto donde se disputa el torneo, impiden que se acceda a los partidos con objetos como aros de luz. El personal acreditado de Wimbledon tiene, además, prohibido grabar vídeo en la mayoría de zonas del club. Durante la disputa del US Open, en uno de los partidos de la cuatro veces ganadora de Grand Slam Naomi Osaka, un grupo de 'influencers' utilizó uno de estos aros de luz, distrayendo a las jugadoras, además de que el juez de silla tuvo que llamar la atención al público en varias ocasiones. La japonesa criticó esta actitud, mientras que Coco Gauff animó a que se sigan las reglas de etiqueta del deporte. También ha habido otro tipo de interrupciones durante algunos encuentros de esta edición del US Open. Aryna Sabalenka, número uno del mundo, paró un partido porque supuestamente alguien estaba fumando marihuana en la grada.

Her background in design has also supported her work in fashion and branding.The couple’s wealth could continue to grow. Paul remains an important part of the new generation of American tennis players, while Lorenze continues to expand her digital and business presence. articles.title: US Open today: Day 10 quarterfinal schedule, scores; Day 11 matchups
articles.summary: The 2026 US Open heads to the quarterfinals, featuring many top seeds competing for places in the men’s and women’s singles semifinals.
articles.body:
The 2026 US Open heads into the quarterfinal stage on Tuesday, Sept. 8, showcasing many of the tournament's top seeds battling for a spot in both the men's and women's singles semifinals.

The day kicks off with the first women's singles quarterfinal, featuring Wworld No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka , who is aiming for her fourth US Open title. She will take on Wimbledon champion and No. 6 seed Linda Noskova , who endured a tense battle against Marta Kostyuk – requiring six match points – to ultimately secure her spot in the quarterfinals.

The second women's quarterfinal sets the stage for an all-American showdown between No. 3 seed Jessica Pegula and No. 26 seed Emma Navarro .

Turning to the men's draw, fans will see another all-American battle as No. 11 seed Frances Tiafoe faces off against the unseeded Alex Michelsen .

The evening session will culminate with a marquee matchup as defending champion Carlos Alcaraz, the No. 2 seed, takes on No. 8 seed Ben Shelton.

Unforgettable US Open 2026 tennis photos from New York

articles.title: US Open: Mirra Andreeva rushes to injured friend Anastasia Potapova’s aid in touching moment
articles.summary: Tennis News: NEW YORK CITY: Anastasia Potapova clutched her knee and crumpled to the court in the closing stages of a gruelling US Open fourth-round clash. After t.
articles.body: NEW YORK CITY: Anastasia Potapova clutched her knee and crumpled to the court in the closing stages of a gruelling US Open fourth-round clash. After two hours and 25 minutes of pushing each other to their limits, the moment the 25-year-old went down, Mirra Andreeva, the No.5 seed, sprinted across the court to help her friend.In the end, Andreeva, the reigning Roland Garros champion, won the last game to seal a 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 victory, but it was her rush to Potapova’s aid that lingered long after the match.Andreeva, 19, first met Potapova in Monastir, Tunisia when she was handed a wildcard into the WTA 250 and drew Potapova in the first round. At the time, she was already an established name on tour and, to Andreeva, a player she had watched from afar.“Nastya was always like a prodigy. She came on tour early, she also had a lot of wins,” Andreeva recalled.Potapova won that first meeting, but Andreeva came away impressed by more than her tennis.“She said a lot of nice words,” Andreeva said. The two began practising together and, as they spent more time around each other, their friendship grew naturally.In the quarterfinals, Andreeva will play world No.4 Coco Gauff.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Holger Rune volverá a competir con Dinamarca en la Copa Davis
articles.standfirst: El danés se rompió el tendón de Aquiles hace 11 meses en las semifinales de Estocolmo
articles.summary: El danés se rompió el tendón de Aquiles hace 11 meses en las semifinales de Estocolmo
articles.body: Holger Rune está de vuelta. Pasados 11 meses desde que se rompió el tendón de Aquiles en las semifinales de Estocolmo con Ugo Humbert, el danés ha anunciado que jugará la serie de Copa Davis entre Dinamarca y Bulgaria, del 18 al 20 de septiembre. Rune, de 23 años y que ha caído al puesto 133 de las listas ATP, tendrá nueve torneos donde podrá utilizar su ranking protegido. La última vez que se vio entrenar al danés fue en Murcia al lado de Carlos Alcaraz, en la puesta a punto del campeón de siete grandes para el Abierto de los Estados Unidos. Carlitos tomó un vuelo a Nueva York, pero su improvisado 'sparring' se quedó en tierra. Rune tenía previsto volver a la competición oficial el pasado mes de mayo en el Open 500 de Hamburgo. Ha ido retrasando su regreso hasta mediados de septiembre para tener plenas garantías de no recaer.

articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton have both become major young stars in men’s tennis, but their careers have taken very different paths so far. Alcaraz has already won seven Grand Slam titles and built a huge following around the world, while Shelton is still working his way up as one of the top American players. Their difference in experience is also clear when it comes to their finances, with Alcaraz’s net worth estimated at around $50–60 million in 2026, compared with roughly $4 million for Shelton.Carlos Alcaraz vs Ben Shelton net worth and earnings: Who is richer?Alcaraz has built a much larger fortune through both tennis prize money and endorsement deals. His career prize money is around $65 million, while his 12-month on-court earnings were reported at about $15.7 million.His off-court income is even more impressive. Forbes estimated Alcaraz’s earnings outside tennis at around $38 million over the 12 months to mid-2026. His biggest partnerships include Nike, Rolex, BMW, Louis Vuitton, Babolat, Infosys and Ant International.Shelton has also built a strong income for a player at his stage of his career. His career prize money has passed $13.3 million, with more than $1.8 million coming during the 2026 season. His endorsement portfolio includes Rolex, On Running, Yonex, Loewe, Ralph Lauren, Thorne Health and Bose.CategoryCarlos AlcarazBen SheltonEstimated net worth$50–60 million~$4 millionCareer prize money~$65 million$13.3+ million2026 season prize money—$1.8+ million12-month off-court earnings~$38 million~$1.5–2 million estimatedGrand Slam titles70Career Grand SlamYesNoCareer-high rankingWorld No. 1World No. 5Major brandsNike, Rolex, BMW, Louis VuittonRolex, On Running, Yonex, LoeweCarlos Alcaraz vs Ben Shelton: Awards, titles and tennis achievementsThis is where Alcaraz has the biggest advantage. The Spaniard has already collected seven Grand Slam singles titles and completed the Career Grand Slam at just 22. He has also won multiple ATP Masters 1000 titles and spent significant time near the top of the rankings.Shelton has yet to win a Grand Slam, but his rise has been impressive. He reached the 2023 US Open and 2025 Australian Open semifinals and reached a career-high ranking of No. 5.In 2026, Shelton added major titles in Dallas, Munich and Stuttgart, while his Munich victory made him the first American man since Andre Agassi in 2002 to win an ATP 500-level clay title.Carlos Alcaraz vs Ben Shelton: Lifestyle and endorsementsAlcaraz’s growing wealth has brought him a more luxurious public image. He owns property in Spain and regularly appears alongside major luxury brands such as Rolex, BMW and Louis Vuitton. His global profile has also opened the door to high-paying exhibitions and appearances.Shelton’s lifestyle is still centered around life on the ATP Tour, but his growing popularity is creating new opportunities. His relationship with USWNT star Trinity Rodman has attracted plenty of attention, while projects such as his YouTube series and Netflix appearance are helping him build a brand away from tennis.For now, Carlos Alcaraz is comfortably ahead in both wealth and career achievements. articles.summary: Las magníficas instalaciones del Club Atlético Montemar, en Alicante, acogieron con éxito la vigésimo quinta prueba del Circuito Juvenil RPT - Marca by Wilson powered by Ambrosía, con las categorías Cadete - Sub16 y Junior - Sub18, del Circuito Juvenil más longevo del Tenis Español, que este año celebra su trigésimo primer aniversario, organizado por el Registro Profesional de Tenis.
articles.body: Las magníficas instalaciones del Club Atlético Montemar, en Alicante, acogieron con éxito la vigésimo quinta prueba del Circuito Juvenil RPT - Marca by Wilson powered by Ambrosía, con las categorías Cadete - Sub16 y Junior - Sub18, del Circuito Juvenil más longevo del Tenis Español, que este año celebra su trigésimo primer aniversario, organizado por el Registro Profesional de Tenis. Está prueba cumplió este año 15 años consecutivos en el Club Atlético Montemar y estuvo dirigida por Jesús Monzó, actuando de juez árbitro José Gimeno, que coordinaron a los cerca de 150 participantes de toda la geografía española. Está prueba cuenta con el apoyo de la Real Federación Española de Tenis y de la Federación de Tenis de la Comunidad Valenciana. En la entrega de premios estuvieron presentes Jesús Monzó, José Gimeno y Luis Mediero. Los resultados de las finales han sido los siguientes: Categoría Jóvenes Promesas U16: Final Masculina Sub16: Jorge Garceran (1) gana a José M. Paulsen por 3/6 7/5 7/6. Final Femenina Sub16: Mariia Panasyuk (2) gana a Siena Wanting por 6/1 6/2. Categoría Junior Cup Challenge U18 Final Masculina Sub18: Sergio Esquerdo (2) gana a Pascual Gozalvo por 6/4 6/3. Final Femenina Sub18: Irene Osorio (2) gana a Sofia Garcia de Freitas por 6/4 6/0. Además, coincidiendo con las rondas finales del torneo se impartieron diferentes cursos de formación y certificación profesional para monitores y entrenadores de tenis, organizados por el Registro Profesional de Tenis, que fueron dirigidos por Luis Mediero. El Registro Profesional de Tenis - RPT es el más antiguo y mayor promotor del Tenis Juvenil en España, organizando desde 1995 el Circuito Nacional RPT - MARCA by Wilson powered by Ambrosía, que en su 31° edición tendrá 31 semanas de competición con 89 pruebas por toda la geografía española, con el apoyo de la Real Federación Española de Tenis, y la colaboración de Ambrosía, NH hotels, HdI, ICI Sports University y APE deporte. Este año se estima que participen en el Circuito más de 6.000 jugadores. Ya puedes consultar el calendario 2026 en la nueva web: torneos.icisports.org

articles.title: Can Carlos Alcaraz shatter all three Americans' dreams' on his way while defending his US Open crown?
articles.summary: International Sports News: Carlos Alcaraz could find himself in a fascinating battle against an entire nation at the US Open. The Spanish superstar is just three wins away from .
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz could find himself in a fascinating battle against an entire nation at the US Open. The Spanish superstar is just three wins away from defending his title. But standing in his way are three American stars, Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen. All three are in his half of the draw. Alcaraz faces Shelton in the quarter-finals on Tuesday. If he wins, he will meet either Tiafoe or Michelsen in the semi-finals.For American tennis fans, the stakes could hardly be higher. The United States has not produced a men’s singles champion at Flushing Meadows since Andy Roddick lifted the trophy in 2003. Alcaraz could personally end the hopes of all three remaining American contenders before reaching the final. He knows the Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd will be firmly behind his opponents.Can Carlos Alcaraz silence America’s dream of a home champion at US Open Carlos Alcaraz has been handed a difficult path to the US Open final.The defending champion first has to deal with Ben Shelton. The 23-year-old American is looking to reach his second US Open semi-final. More importantly, he is chasing his first career victory over Alcaraz.Shelton will have one major advantage. The Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd.Alcaraz expects the packed New York crowd to make life difficult. He knows Shelton will feed off the support from the stands. But Alcaraz has already shown that he can handle big occasions.The seven-time Grand Slam champion is now just three victories away from successfully defending his US Open crown. Yet his route to the trophy could become a Spanish-American showdown.If he defeats Shelton, Alcaraz will meet either Frances Tiafoe or Alex Michelsen.Tiafoe is no stranger to the biggest stage in New York. The 28-year-old reached the US Open semi-finals in 2022 and 2024. He lost to Alcaraz in the last four three years ago.He is now chasing a third chance to reach his first Grand Slam final.Tiafoe has also arrived in New York with confidence. He reached the Cincinnati final last month and has continued to enjoy the energy of the home crowd.Michelsen presents a different challenge. The 22-year-old has quietly moved through the draw without dropping a set. He has reached a Grand Slam quarter-final for the first time.The world number 46 admitted he was happy to remain “under the radar”. That will now change.American tennis has enjoyed a strong run at this year’s US Open. Six American men and women have reached the quarter-finals, the country’s highest combined tally since 2002.But the men’s title drought remains. Since Roddick’s 2003 triumph, Taylor Fritz is the only American man to reach the US Open final. He lost to Jannik Sinner in 2024.Now Alcaraz stands directly between three American stars and another potential final.If he beats Shelton, then Tiafoe or Michelsen, the Spaniard could silence the American charge before playing for another title.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rafael Nadal’s inspiring family story: How Toni and Miguel Angel Nadal shaped his legendary tennis journey, discipline, humility and success in 22 Grand Slam titles
articles.summary: International Sports News: Explore how Rafa Nadal's uncles Toni and Miguel Angel shaped his journey to becoming a tennis legend, instilling discipline, humility, and the values that led to his success.
articles.body: Rafael Nadal has enjoyed an amazing tennis career, thanks to amazing talent, physical stamina and a competitive spirit like no other. The personality of the 22-time Grand Slam champion was shaped from a young age by a close family in Mallorca, in particular the influence of his uncles Toni Nadal and Miguel Angel Nadal.The Nadal family had influence beyond tennis. Toni was demanding in coaching, instilling lessons in discipline, while Miguel Angel was an example of elite football, professionalism and sporting success. With his parents, Sebastián Nadal and Ana María Parera, the family helped keep the future champion grounded as his fame spread across the globe.How Rafael Nadal’s family shaped his legendary tennis careerNadal’s rise began in Manacor, Mallorca, where tennis was a key part of his childhood. His uncle Toni soon recognised his nephew’s unusual instinct on the court and became the coach who would influence much of his development. Toni worked with Nadal from childhood until 2017 and was in his corner for 16 of his 22 Grand Slam titles.Toni’s methods were tough. Training included repeated practice, physical exertion and an emphasis on concentration, responsibility and improvement. In those days, Nadal’s job was to retrieve tennis balls and tend to his equipment, with junior-level victories regarded as stepping stones rather than reasons to party.The family also opted for stability rather than a quick exit from Mallorca. When Nadal was 14, the family turned down a tennis scholarship that would have required them to move to Barcelona, allowing him to continue to develop in his familiar home environment and coaching framework.How Miguel Angel Nadal influenced Rafael Nadal’s sporting journeyToni Nadal had a direct hand in shaping Rafael’s tennis, but Miguel Angel Nadal was another powerful sporting influence. Miguel Angel, a former defender for FC Barcelona and Spain, was already an established elite athlete before Rafael became a global tennis star. His presence provided the young Nadal with an example of what professional sport required away from the spotlight.Miguel Angel’s career also mirrored the larger athletic milieu that surrounded the Nadal family. It is said Rafael was interested in football as a boy and that his uncle’s footballing success gave him the chance to see top-level competition first-hand. Nadal’s football connection was also a feature of his early sporting identity, before tennis became his clear professional path.Miguel Angel’s role was therefore more than that of a direct coach. He was the family’s established sporting benchmark, demonstrating to Rafael the pressures, discipline and responsibilities of elite sport. Rafael grew up in an atmosphere of professional commitment, as both Toni and Miguel Angel had a background in competitive sport.How Nadal family values shaped Rafael Nadal’s legacyPerhaps the greatest contribution of the Nadal family was to stress the importance of staying grounded. But his family in Mallorca continued to provide the usual surroundings even as Rafael began winning major titles and international recognition. His parents, Sebastián and Ana María, were important people in his life, and his sister Maribel and other family members were part of his support system.Family influenceImpact on Rafael NadalToni NadalDiscipline, endurance, competitiveness and mental strengthMiguel Angel NadalElite sporting example and football influenceSebastián NadalStability and family supportAna María PareraStrong family foundation and personal groundingMaribel NadalClose sibling support and connection to home22 Grand Slam titles are the headline achievement, but the deeper story is the family structure behind the achievement. Toni’s tough lessons, the sporting example of Miguel Angel and the wider Nadal family’s emphasis on humility helped shape a champion whose legacy is more than just trophies.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: US Open predictions and expert picks for tournament's quarterfinal round
articles.summary: Our experts predict how the US Open quarterfinal round will unfold, including which American stars will move on to the semifinals.
articles.body:
The 2026 US Open reaches the quarterfinals having delivered everything tennis fans could ask for: dramatic upsets, breakout performances and championship-caliber battles under the lights in New York.

Now, with the tournament entering its final stages, attention turns to the biggest question of all: Who will leave Flushing Meadows with a Grand Slam title?

From tournament favorites and proven champions to dangerous dark horses capable of bigger surprises, our experts give their takes on the men's and women's draws with predictions of the quarterfinal round:

Unforgettable US Open 2026 tennis photos from New York

US Open predictions in women's quarterfinals

There is no reason to get away from previous predictions: Americans Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula will be in the semifinals.

Pegula will dispatch fellow American Emma Navarro in the quarterfinals to set up a date with current Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the semfinals. Noskova will knock out two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka and be partly responsible for Sabalenka losing her No. 1 ranking.

Coco Gauff , meanwhile, will prevail against Mirra Andreeva in a battle of the past two French Open champions, setting up a semifinal match against newly top-ranked Elena Rybakina , the reigning Australian Open champion.

Aryna Sabalenka hasn't dropped a set yet in this tournament, but that streak – and her chance at a U.S. Open three-peat – will end when she loses to this year's Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova . Noskova, as she often does, will come out strong in the first set and lose the second set before bouncing back to defeat Sabalenka and clinch a spot in the U.S. Open semifinals for the first time in her career.

In more bad news for Sabalenka, Elena Rybakina will take over the No. 1 ranking from Sabalenka when she reaches the semifinals by dispatching Qinwen Zhang .

Meanwhile, the two highest ranked American women will both reach the semis as world No. 3 Jessica Pegula takes care of Emma Navarro and world No. 4 Coco Gauff remains undefeated against Mirra Andreeva in their sixth meeting.

US Open predictions in men's quarterfinals

Since the men's draw is more unpredictable, with only three of the 10 seeds making the fourth round, two-time US Open winner Carlos Alcaraz (2022, 2025) is the pick here over Ben Shelton . U.S. fans will still have an American contender, though, as Frances Tiafoe reaches his third US Open semifinal (2022, 2024) after ending Alex Michelsen's longshot bid.

On the other side of the draw, No. 1 Alexander Zverev will continue to cruise, dispatching an exhausted Botic van de Zandschulp , who needed five sets and three tiebreakers Monday to even reach the quarterfinals. Unseeded Karen Khachanov will notch another upset, taking down No. 28 Alexander Blockx , to set up a semifinal clash with Zverev.

Although Ben Shelton has looked like the strongest American contender on the men's side, he won't get past the unflappable defending U.S. Open champion Carlos Alcaraz , who has never dropped a set to Shelton in two previous hard-court meetings. But Alcarez will face another American in the semifinals after Frances Tiafoe ends Alex Michelsen's Cinderella run .

No. 1 seed and late-night session king Alexander Zverev will outlast giant slayer Botic van de Zandschulp . Belgian Alexander Blockx will attempt to battle through his rib injury but ultimately succumb to Karen Khachanov , who will reach his third major semifinal (2022 U.S. Open, 2023 Australian Open).

articles.title: No. 1 in reach as Rybakina battles for US Open semi-final spot
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina is one win away from the world number one ranking, but the Kazakh star says her main goal in her US Open quarter-final clash with Zheng Qinwen...
articles.body:
Elena Rybakina is one win away from the world number one ranking, but the Kazakh star says her main goal in her US Open quarter-final clash with Zheng Qinwen on Wednesday is to advance toward a third Grand Slam title.

"Number one ranking is, of course, one of the goals," Rybakina says. "But I think the main focus for me is to win the titles, and then the ranking will follow up."

Rybakina arrived at Flushing Meadows as one of four women with a chance to supplant Aryna Sabalenka atop the rankings, and the only one with her fate in her own hands. Reaching the semis will send her to the summit for the first time, and she could even get there if she loses -- if Sabalenka, world number three Jessica Pegula and fourth-ranked Coco Gauff all fail to lift the trophy.

Rybakina, who has shown no sign of the foot injury that hindered her US Open preparations, will be out to halt the remarkable run of Zheng -- the Paris Olympics gold medallist who had to come through qualifying thanks to a rankings plunge in the wake of elbow surgery last year.

Gauff, in the quarters for the first time since she won the US Open title in 2023, will take on fifth-seeded French Open champion Mirra Andreeva for a place in the semis while men's top seed Alexander Zverev faces Dutch veteran Botic van de Zandschulp.

Alexander Blockx tries to further his dream US Open debut taking on Russian Karen Khachanov.

AFP Sport looks at Wednesday's action at the US Open

Elena Rybakina (KAZ x2) v Zheng Qinwen (CHN)

Rybakina's four victories over Zheng include two this year, but the former world number one from China is finally on a roll. Counting qualifying Zheng has racked up seven wins in Flushing Meadows, including a dramatic come-from-behind victory over Madison Keys in which she saved a match point as she rallied from 5-0 down in the third set to win with closing run of seven straight games.

She followed with another seven-game surge to salvage the first set in a straight-sets victory over six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek.

"She definitely found her form," Rybakina said. "I feel like she's playing now with a lot of confidence after so many wins in a row, so she's very dangerous."

Coco Gauff (USA x4) v Mirra Andreeva (RUS x5)

Gauff has won all five meetings with the fifth-seeded French Open champion, including a victory on the way to the 2023 US Open title and, most recently, a win in the quarter-finals in Rome.

That was before Andreeva broke through for her first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros, and Gauff believes that triumph means she'll be facing a new Andreeva.

"She's obviously in a different mindset now at the top of the game coming off of a Grand Slam win," Gauff said. "I expect her to approach the match completely differently.

"I think it's going to be a really athletic, tough match. Hopefully I can take my opportunities when I get them."

Alexander Zverev (GER x1) v Botic van de Zandschulp (NED)

World number two Zverev knows the 70th-ranked van de Zandschulp is a tricky proposition on the US Open hard courts, where the Dutch player stunned then world number three Carlos Alcaraz in the second round two years ago.

"I think he's an impressive player," Zverev said. "I think this might be his favorite tournament in the world ... Obviously he knows how to play well on these courts"

Zverev himself was slow to fire in Flushing Meadows, laboring through two five-setters to start the tournament before straightforward wins over seeded players Alejandro Tabilo and Luciano Darderi.

"I think after 10 hours on court, I just maybe found my rhythm a little bit better, which is helpful because the first two matches were really not great level," said Zverev, who claimed a long awaited maiden Grand Slam at Roland Garros.

Karen Khachanov (RUS) v Alexander Blockx (BEL x28)

It's a race for fitness for 21-year-old Blockx, who nearly retired from his fourth-round win over Francisco Cerundolo because of a painful rib injury. With the help of mid-match medication he soldiered on, saving 14 of 17 break points he faced and striking 36 winners.

"I don't know," he said. "Right now at the moment it feels good. I've had some treatment, some medication, so hopefully it stays that way and gets even better tomorrow and (for the) upcoming match. We'll see."

Khachanov will have experience on his side. The Russian, who reached the US Open semi-finals in 2022, booked his seventh major quarter-final with a five-set win over 20-year-old American Learner Tien.
